title: Awarapan 2 Has Wrapped Filming. Emraan Hashmi Returns as Shivam After 19 Years.
excerpt: Disha Patani joins the Vishesh Films sequel, shot across Rajasthan and South East Asia. The Independence Day weekend release is locked.
body:
Vishesh Films has announced the completion of principal photography on *Awarapan 2*, bringing Emraan Hashmi back to the role that turned him into a cult figure nearly two decades ago. The sequel to the 2007 romantic thriller is scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on August 14, 2026 — landing squarely on the Independence Day weekend, one of Bollywood's most coveted release windows.

Hashmi returns as Shivam, the tortured gangster whose doomed love story made the original *Awarapan* a slow-burn hit that outlived its modest box office run. The first film ended with a dream sequence showing Shivam reuniting with his love, played by Shriya Saran. The sequel picks up from that ambiguous final frame. Shivam comes back to life and encounters a new character played by Disha Patani, who joins Vishesh Films for the first time.

## A Sequel 19 Years in the Making

The original *Awarapan*, directed by Mohit Suri, was not a commercial success on release. But its soundtrack — anchored by tracks like *Toh Phir Aao* and *Tera Mera Rishta* composed by Pritam — became defining songs of mid-2000s Bollywood. For the Indian diaspora especially, those songs soundtracked college playlists, road trips, and late-night study sessions across campuses from New Jersey to London. The film found its audience on DVD and television reruns, eventually earning the kind of reverence that studios now build franchises around.

Producer Vishesh Bhatt underlined the scale of the project. "Awarapan is an emotion so large that it's meant for the big screen," he said in a statement. "It presents exotic settings and large-scale sequences, but fundamentally it's built on our core principles of layered storytelling with powerful characters and rich music. Emraan felt the angst of Shivam so deeply that he stepped into character in a heartbeat."

## New Director, New Setting

Nitin Kakkar, known for directing *Jawaani Jaaneman*, takes over the director's chair from Mohit Suri. The screenplay is written by Bilal Siddiqui. The film was shot across Rajasthan and South East Asia, a deliberate departure from the original's Hong Kong setting. Reports indicate that the team completed high-octane action sequences in real locations across Bangkok, followed by extensive Mumbai shoots.

The distributor interest alone signals confidence. Before the wrap announcement, reports surfaced of a distributor frenzy, with Dharma, Zee Studios, AA Films, and others meeting Mukesh Bhatt for theatrical rights — an unusual level of pre-release competition for a mid-budget sequel.

## What It Means for NRIs

For diaspora audiences who grew up on Vishesh Films' moody, music-driven thrillers — from *Aashiqui* to *Murder* to *Gangster* — *Awarapan 2* represents a specific kind of nostalgia. These were not the glossy, song-and-dance spectacles of Yash Raj or Dharma. They were raw, atmospheric, and emotionally charged films that hit differently when watched alone on a laptop in a dorm room ten thousand miles from home.

Whether the sequel can recapture that magic with a new director and a 19-year gap remains to be seen. But the Independence Day release date, Hashmi's return, and the Vishesh Films pedigree suggest the studio is betting big. The collaboration with Sony Music India continues, which means the soundtrack will likely be positioned as a major selling point.

*Awarapan 2* releases in cinemas worldwide on August 14, 2026.
